svg.desc: candidate number: 9; slug: probate-real-estate; title: Probate Real Estate; category: Real estate services; production stage: approved_master; scores: revenue potential: 23; profit margin potential: 18; team efficiency: 16; startup accessibility: 9; automation potential: 10; dimension max: revenue potential: 25; profit margin potential: 25; team efficiency: 20; startup accessibility: 15; automation potential: 15; total score: 76; tier label: High-Leverage Operator Play; evidence confidence: High; uncertainty band: ±3 pts; uncertainty bounds: low: 73; high: 79; uncertainty note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.; score rationale: revenue potential: Revenue Potential: 23/25. Modeled as licensed brokerage rather than capital-heavy property acquisition.; profit margin potential: Profit Margin Potential: 18/25. Modeled as licensed brokerage rather than capital-heavy property acquisition.; team efficiency: Team Efficiency: 16/20. Modeled as licensed brokerage rather than capital-heavy property acquisition.; startup accessibility: Startup Accessibility: 9/15. Modeled as licensed brokerage rather than capital-heavy property acquisition.; automation potential: Automation Potential: 10/15. Modeled as licensed brokerage rather than capital-heavy property acquisition.; economics: gross revenue range: $120,000–$900,000 USD annually; net profit margin range: 20–35%; owner net profit potential: $24,000–$315,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $15,000–$100,000 USD; monthly opex range: $3,000–$18,000 USD; time to first deal: 4–18 months; typical team size: full time including owner: 2; contractors: 3; total people: 5; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Retained brokerage commissions after brokerage splits, not home sale values; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data; scenarios: conservative: annual gross revenue usd: 120000; net profit margin pct: 20; annual owner net profit usd: 24000; full time including owner: 2; contractors: 3; total people: 5; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; base case: annual gross revenue usd: 510000.0; net profit margin pct: 27.5; annual owner net profit usd: 140250; full time including owner: 2; contractors: 3; total people: 5; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; scaled small team: annual gross revenue usd: 900000; net profit margin pct: 35; annual owner net profit usd: 315000; full time including owner: 3; contractors: 4; total people: 7; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Docket alerts; Transaction checklists; key risks: Court delays; Family disputes; Housing-market cycles; regulatory notes: Real estate licensing, fiduciary duties and court-sale approvals may apply.; track ids: track_1; track_2; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; plays: id: public_record_api_intelligence; track id: track_1; name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.; inputs: Court & probate dockets; State controller ledgers; Public licensing & entity APIs; workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence; Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold; Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution; metrics: Cost per verified lead; Docket-to-contact latency (hours); Net recovery / conversion rate; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; id: public_filing_trigger_mail_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: New-LLC & Recorded-Deed Trigger-Mail Arbitrage; mechanism: Ingest daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and County Recorder new-deed/mortgage recordings to trigger programmatic direct mail via API—replacing illegal government-lookalike poster/deed invoices (which violate 39 U.S.C. § 3001 and state deed-solicitation laws) with high-LTV recurring workplace compliance subscriptions, property-tax appeal contingency offers, and exclusive new-mover/B2B lead monetization.; inputs: Daily Secretary of State new-entity (LLC/Corp) bulk feeds; County Recorder grant/warranty deed & mortgage recording dockets; Programmatic print-and-mail API (Lob / PostGrid) + QR intake bridge; workflow: Pull daily new-LLC formations (filtering for employer/commercial NAICS or multi-member filings) and newly recorded residential deeds with purchase price and loan metadata; Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data; Monetize new LLCs via recurring annual labor-poster/registered-agent compliance memberships and B2B partner referrals; monetize new deeds via contingency property-tax appeal filings or high-ticket homeowner lead sales; metrics: Filing-to-mailbox latency (hours); QR scan & intake conversion % per 1,000 mailers; Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece; platform risks: failure mode: USPS 39 U.S.C. § 3001(h)-(i) mail-stop order, State AG UDAP enforcement, or payment-processor freeze; trigger: Styling mailers as fake government penalty notices, invoices, or charging $89-$195 solely for a $3 public deed copy without statutory disclaimers; impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates; detection metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency; fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services); id: rank_and_rent_pay_per_call_routing; track id: track_2; name: Rank-and-Rent Digital Real Estate & Pay-Per-Call Routing; mechanism: Build and rank local high-ticket service hubs (foundation repair, water restoration, probate liquidation, commercial roofing) wired to dynamic call-tracking switches (Ringba / Twilio) that auto-bill local operators $75–$300 per inbound call lasting over 90 seconds.; inputs: City + high-ticket emergency/specialty service domain portfolio; Ringba / Twilio dynamic number insertion (DNI) & IVR duration billing switch; Co-verified local contractor partner agreements with card-on-file auto-recharge; workflow: Launch fast programmatic local service pages and cost calculators for high-ticket, high-urgency verticals ($5,000+ average job ticket); Partner with a licensed brick-and-mortar operator in each city for legitimate Google Business Profile co-verification while retaining ownership of the domain and tracking numbers; Route inbound prospect calls through Ringba with a 90-second duration threshold, automatically charging the partner's card on file per qualified call; metrics: Inbound calls per site per month & % of calls >90 seconds; Revenue per qualified call ($75–$300) and contractor retention rate; Portfolio gross margin (80–90% once ranked); platform risks: failure mode: Google Business Profile suspension or contractor payment default; trigger: Registering fake Google Maps pins at UPS stores/virtual offices or delivering calls before collecting prepaid credit balances; impact: Loss of Map Pack call volume or uncollected call receivables; detection metric: Organic-vs-Maps call split and prepaid Stripe wallet balance per partner; fallback: Anchor traffic in organic city/calculator pages (immune to GBP suspension), co-verify Maps only with real partner physical addresses, and enforce prepaid auto-refill call wallets; id: identity_graph_pixel_arbitrage; track id: track_2; name: Identity-Graph Pixel & Search-Intent Deanonymization; mechanism: Deploy first-party CNAME identity-resolution pixels and pre-click search/bidstream intent feeds (syncing visitor IP/device hashes against publisher co-op SHA-256 rainbow tables and property/B2B graphs) to resolve 35–55% of anonymous bouncing search visitors into verified names, emails, LinkedIn profiles, and physical home addresses.; inputs: First-party CNAME identity-resolution pixel & Google Ads ValueTrack ({keyword}) URL tags; Publisher co-op SHA-256 HEM spine + County Assessor / B2B LinkedIn enrichment graph; Automated physical postcard API (Lob / PostGrid), B2B Slack routing, & Custom Audience sync; workflow: Geo-fence pixel execution at the CDN edge (US-only, excluding EU/UK GDPR traffic) and capture exact referring search keywords via ValueTrack parameters; Resolve anonymous bouncing visitors against the identity spine within 200ms to append homeowner address, work email, and LinkedIn URL; Route resolved B2B executives to instant Slack/LinkedIn warm outreach, trigger physical next-day postcards to resolved homeowner addresses, and sync SHA-256 hashes into Meta/Google Custom Audiences; metrics: Anonymous visitor-to-identity match rate (35–55% target); Cost per resolved identity ($0.10–$0.25) vs. net recovered revenue per 1,000 bounces; Postcard & B2B LinkedIn intercept conversion rate (%); platform risks: failure mode: Primary email domain blacklisting (>0.3% spam complaint rate) or California CIPA / state privacy demand letters; trigger: Blasting cold consumer Gmail addresses from primary brand domains saying 'we saw you on our site' or firing third-party pixels without geo-fencing/consent notice; impact: Google Workspace / ESP domain suspension or statutory privacy settlement costs; detection metric: Postmaster Tools spam rate >0.1%, bounce rate >2%, and edge geo-fence block verification; fallback: Never cold-email unconsented consumer Gmail addresses from primary domains; monetize consumer matches strictly via CAN-SPAM-exempt physical trigger mail and SHA-256 ad-audience sync, and enforce US-only edge geo-gating; id: probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping; mechanism: Parse county probate petitions (Letters Testamentary / Letters of Administration) and daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) filings before national aggregators index them, matching out-of-state personal representatives and distressed owners to licensed probate brokers and cash buyers.; inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings; County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds; Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline; workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing; Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records; Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions; metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days); Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%); Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting; trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits; impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement; detection metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges; fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record; id: municipal_code_violation_trigger_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Municipal Code-Violation, Mechanic's Lien & Permit-Failure Lead Arbitrage; mechanism: Poll municipal building department portals and county recorder dockets daily for failed structural/fire inspections, expired permits, code citations, and newly filed mechanic's liens, routing exclusive real-time leads to remediation contractors and construction attorneys.; inputs: Municipal Accela/EnerGov building & code-enforcement portals; County recorder mechanic's lien & lis pendens dockets; Real-time Pay-Per-Call & exclusive CPL routing switch; workflow: Scrape and normalize daily municipal code citations, failed permit inspections, and recorded mechanic's liens across target metro counties; Enrich parcel owner contact records and classify urgency by abatement deadline or fine accrual rate; Route verified property owners via direct mail/outbound alerts into exclusive Pay-Per-Call or CPL agreements with licensed remediation contractors; metrics: Citation-to-outreach latency (hours); Qualified homeowner/commercial call conversion %; Revenue per exclusive routed remediation lead; platform risks: failure mode: Municipal portal IP blocking or deceptive official-notice complaints; trigger: Aggressive unthrottled scraping of Accela/EnerGov portals or styling outreach like an official city abatement order; impact: Portal IP block or city attorney cease-and-desist notice; detection metric: Portal HTTP 403/429 rate and zero municipal impersonation complaints; fallback: Use low-frequency scheduled API/bulk exports and clearly identify all outreach as private commercial contractor/remediation assistance; id: property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency; track id: track_1; name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage; mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.; inputs: Annual county tax-assessor preliminary valuation rolls & parcel GIS characteristics; Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine; Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline; workflow: Ingest county assessment rolls the day annual valuation notices drop and compute each parcel's assessed-per-sqft percentile against direct neighborhood peers; Mail personalized pre-filled protest postcards showing the owner's exact estimated over-assessment and a QR code to sign a zero-upfront-cost contingency authorization; Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings; metrics: Protest-window mail-to-signed-authorization conversion %; Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target); Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State property-tax consultant licensing requirements or missed county protest bar dates; trigger: Representing property owners for a fee without required state registration (e.g., Texas TDLR Property Tax Consultant license) or missing the 30/45-day county filing deadline; impact: Rejected bulk filings, administrative fines, or zero contingency revenue for the tax year; detection metric: 100% licensed tax-agent sign-off in regulated states and T-minus-7-day bulk filing completion; fallback: Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants/attorneys of record in regulated states and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing; id: google_maps_gbp_lead_gen_network; track id: track_2; name: Multi-Location Google Business Profile (GBP) Local-Pack Grid Arbitrage; mechanism: Capture high-margin Google Maps 3-Pack calls across tier-2/3 metros by partnering with real, licensed local tradespeople to co-verify legitimate physical office/shop locations, wiring call-tracking numbers and review-automation workflows to monetize excess lead capacity.; inputs: Geo-grid rank tracker identifying low-review-count Map Pack gaps in $3k+ home/commercial verticals; Joint-venture co-verification agreements with real brick-and-mortar licensed contractors; Dynamic call routing (Ringba) + automated SMS post-job review velocity loop; workflow: Identify suburban and tier-2 metro sub-markets where top-3 Google Maps competitors have <40 reviews and weak category optimization; Sign a revenue-share or pay-per-call partnership with a real local contractor or commercial office tenant (never using fake UPS boxes or virtual coworking addresses); Optimize GBP primary/secondary categories, service-area pages, and automated customer review requests to lock top-3 Map Pack placement and bill per qualified call; metrics: Local Geo-Grid Top-3 share of voice (%); Qualified inbound Map Pack calls per location per month; Net revenue per location ($1,500–$6,000/mo) and partner retention; platform risks: failure mode: Google Business Profile video-verification failure or network-wide account suspension; trigger: Creating fake storefront listings at UPS stores, virtual offices, or residential addresses without signage/licensing; impact: Immediate GBP suspension and loss of all accumulated reviews and Map Pack calls; detection metric: 100% physical signage, utility bill, and state contractor license verification readiness per profile; fallback: Only launch GBP profiles backed by a real partner's physical shop/yard capable of passing live video verification, and pair every listing with organic city rank-and-rent pages; id: hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage; mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.; inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records; Title report and statutory redemption calendar; Local counsel priority and notice opinion; workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility; 2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions; 3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline; 4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire; metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs; Capital days outstanding; Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate; platform risks: failure mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien; trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority; impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation; detection metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition; fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests; id: gis_landlocked_parcel_easement_assemblage; track id: track_1; name: GIS Landlocked-Parcel Spite-Strip & Access-Easement Assemblage Arbitrage; mechanism: Combine GIS parcel geometry with recorded access rights to option overlooked strips and negotiate voluntary easement assemblages; mapped boundaries alone do not establish legal access.; inputs: County GIS parcel and road layers; Recorded plats, deeds, and easement instruments; Surveyor estimates and neighboring-owner demand; workflow: 1. Flag apparently landlocked parcels and narrow connecting strips in GIS; 2. Verify boundaries, existing rights, and easement-by-necessity exposure with surveyor and counsel; 3. Secure contingent options and negotiate voluntary access agreements without obstructing existing access; 4. Record approved easements and close the assembled sale through title escrow; metrics: Verified access gaps per screened parcel; Option-to-recorded-easement conversion rate; Net assemblage margin after survey and title costs; platform risks: failure mode: GIS false positive or unenforceable access premium; trigger: Unmapped easement, boundary error, or preexisting legal right of access; impact: Option expiry or acquisition with no incremental assemblage value; detection metric: Survey and title exceptions per shortlisted parcel; fallback: Exercise diligence contingencies and offer survey-backed voluntary access services instead; id: fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing; track id: track_1; name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing; mechanism: Acquire documented fractional heir interests at a discount reflecting illiquidity, then seek consensual buyouts or counsel-supervised partition subject to heirs-property protections and co-owner rights.; inputs: Probate files and verified heirship records; Title chain, occupancy facts, and independent appraisal; Applicable partition and heirs-property protection rules; workflow: 1. Establish ownership fractions, probate authority, and encumbrances before contacting sellers; 2. Provide transparent offers with independent-advice opportunity and modeled partition costs; 3. Seek voluntary co-owner buyouts or an agreed market sale before considering litigation; 4. If unresolved, use counsel-led statutory procedures honoring notice, appraisal, and buyout rights; metrics: Verified ownership share acquired; Consensual resolution rate; Net proceeds after carrying and legal costs; platform risks: failure mode: Heirs-property protections defeat assumed forced-sale economics; trigger: Mandatory co-owner buyout, partition-in-kind preference, or defective heirship; impact: Long holding period and lower realizable value; detection metric: Unresolved heirs and statutory buyout conditions per property; fallback: Renegotiate voluntary exits or retain the interest without threatening unavailable remedies; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; play id: public_record_api_intelligence; play name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates; detection metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency; fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services); text.title: gross revenue range: $120,000–$900,000 USD annually; net profit margin range: 20–35%; owner net profit potential: $24,000–$315,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $15,000–$100,000 USD; monthly opex range: $3,000–$18,000 USD; time to first deal: 4–18 months; typical team size: full time including owner: 2; contractors: 3; total people: 5; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Retained brokerage commissions after brokerage splits, not home sale values; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data
